subject.title: Telegram delivery should be idempotent across message.send, final replies, and resumed turns

question: Should a successful same-source message tool send in automatic reply mode become authoritative and suppress an equivalent final reply, or should that behavior remain limited to message-tool-only mode and proven recovery replays?
rationale: Current main intentionally terminalizes successful source sends only in message-tool-only mode; broadening this changes delivery semantics and could suppress intentional follow-up output.

options.title: Keep mode-scoped semantics
options.body: Retain automatic final delivery, use message-tool-only mode when explicit sends replace finals, and repair only concretely reproduced retry or resume replay defects.

options.title: Make explicit sends authoritative
options.body: Suppress later same-turn source finals after successful same-source sends in automatic mode, with explicit intentional-follow-up semantics and compatibility proof.

options.title: Add global receipt dedupe
options.body: Persist a logical-result receipt shared across send, final, mirror, retry, and resume paths, accepting a larger state model and false-suppression risk.

recommendation.title: Keep mode-scoped semantics
recommendation.body: Retain automatic final delivery, use message-tool-only mode when explicit sends replace finals, and repair only concretely reproduced retry or resume replay defects.
